findings.claim: At 1 CN the scan fragment is bound by the 4-thread pipeline pool, not by memory or by GPU work: all 107 (q01) / 65 (q06) scan tasks are created within 9-50 ms and wait FIFO for one of 4 slots, the 4 slots are busy for 98%+ of the fragment wall, the memory gate never binds, and each slot is one serial read+decode stream (~5 GB/s in q06), while the same storage delivered 2.5x more aggregate bandwidth to 16 slots on 4 CNs. The CN launcher cannot raise pipeline.num_threads because the derived config emits no pipeline block and overrides --sirius-config.

findings.claim: All six 1-CN failures (q05 q08 q09 q17 q18 q21) are one FE plan shape: an unfiltered lineitem FileScanNode feeding a HASH_PARTITIONED exchange (PARTITIONED join with lineitem on one side). Because nothing streams across a fragment boundary, the CN must park the whole projected lineitem (6.0e9 rows x 28-76 B = 168-456 GB) on a 100 GiB pool; the leaf scan fragment (inputs=0/outputs=1) dies with GPU_SCAN OOM after 100 futile reschedules. Standalone Sirius on the same GPU/pool runs all six in 2.7-6.4 s because DuckDB streams lineitem as the probe of hash joins built on the small filtered dimension chains.

findings.proposed_change: PC-2 fixes both directions. Available today per query: StarRocks join hints `JOIN [BROADCAST]` / `[SHUFFLE]` (parsed in FE sql/parser/AstBuilder.java:6567; HINT_JOIN_BROADCAST zeroes the child cost in EnforceAndCostTask.java:291-296) — e.g. keep `[BROADCAST]` on q03's orders⋈customer side and q12's lineitem side, `[SHUFFLE]` on q07's customer and q02's subquery side. Global knobs are blunt: SET broadcast_row_limit=0 forces shuffle for every non-cross join (EnforceAndCostTask.java:312-314), which helps q22/q07/q02 but hurts q03/q12/q19. A CN-side alternative for the still-broadcast cases: the receiver already knows exact parked rows before build() (engine.rs:562-595); it cannot change the FE cut, so refusing a broadcast there would only fail the query — not recommended.

findings.claim: The FE puts the subquery side of every LEFT SEMI / LEFT ANTI join on the build side and never commutes to RIGHT SEMI/ANTI (q04 builds on 3.79B lineitem rows against a 57M-row orders probe; q22 builds on 1.5B orders rows against 6M customers, broadcast to every CN on 4 CN). Neither the engine nor the translator can repair this: DuckDB's join-order optimizer swaps children only for inner joins and swaps semi/anti back, Sirius builds on children[1], and the translator refuses RIGHT_SEMI_JOIN outright.

findings.claim: The CN's receiver-first exact cardinality declaration works as designed (every declared stream count equals the actual parked rows) and lets DuckDB reorder inner joins inside a fragment, but it cannot influence the FE's fragment cut, semi/anti sides, or FILES() scans inside the same fragment (STATISTICS_PROPAGATION is disabled, so a filtered part scan keeps its raw 200M-row estimate against an exact 128.6M-row lineitem stream in q19). Its cost is the rendezvous itself: the receiver waits for every sender to finish, so small leaf fragments dwell for the whole scan (q02 region/nation fragments wall 0.96-1.02 s with 2-43 ms of compute).

findings.claim: Ranked options and what StarRocks session variables can and cannot do today. No global session variable fixes the plans: broadcast_row_limit / broadcast_right_table_scale_factor never trigger at cardinality 1 (setting the limit to 0 forces shuffle for all non-forced joins, trading q22/q07/q02 broadcasts for q03/q12/q19 regressions); enable_local_shuffle_agg prunes only aggregate exchanges in join-free trees; cbo_cte_reuse_rate=0 forces CTE reuse but the CN rejects the multicast sink; join hints work per query. findings.proposed_change: No transport/arena tuning for this family. Instead: (1) let the receiver fragment start when its build-side streams are complete and consume probe-side streams incrementally (probe-side batches do not need the full-cardinality declaration), which would overlap q04's 30.8 GB lineitem park with the join and remove the per-fragment serialization visible as 0.3-3.8 s of parked dwell; (2) carry the fixes in SAJ-1..3 so the big table is never the exchanged side. result.reasoning:
Every measured number in OOM-2 re-derives from the evidence files, and the mechanism is confirmed in source; no other query or arm contradicts it.

MECHANISM (source, /home/prestouser/aocsa/sirius-stacks-wt/perf): engine.rs:278-280 `while let Ok(request) = requests.recv()` — one EngineRequest at a time; engine.rs:82 comment "a request queued here waits for whatever fragment the engine thread is running". run_fragment_inner (engine.rs:486-720) does declare -> build(&plan) -> relay_from each parked sender -> run() -> park (engine.rs:697-716 inserts ParkedOutput after run). sirius_ffi.cpp:739-745 relay_from throws unless `source.impl_->ran`. local_exchange.rs:248-283 take_ready returns None until `complete == expected` for every input node; SenderSource::LocalParked is_complete()==true by construction, Remote only once eos. Remote path is also park-then-export: EngineRequest::ExportNext drains the parked fragment (engine.rs:91-95, fragment_executor.rs:207-210). WHAT THE CODE DOES (measured/confirmed):
1. Plan shape. In all six FE plans the failing leaf is an unfiltered lineitem FileScanNode under a HASH_PARTITIONED TDataStreamSink (survey/explain: q05 F06 l_orderkey->exch 9; q08 F02 l_partkey->exch 4; q09 F02 l_partkey->exch 4; q17 F00 l_partkey->exch 1; q18 F04 l_orderkey->exch 10; q21 F08 l_orderkey->exch 13; predicates empty in every case). cn1/cluster.log pairs each 'fragment run failed' with a 'fragment run started ... inputs=0 outputs=1' line (4200/6051, 7854/9471, 9840/11963, 16770/17712, 18095/18483, 20282/21345), all with 'exceeded maximum retry limit (100) ... OOM at operator GPU_SCAN (index 0)'. cn1-quent.txt operator lists identify the failing instances as the raw-scan fragments (GPU_SCAN + STREAMING_SINK only; q08 adds a PROJECTION).
2. Nothing streams across a fragment boundary. local_exchange.rs: receiver-first rendezvous, SenderSource::LocalParked::is_complete() is true only once the sender fragment has finished; compute_node_service.rs ~1180: 'The sender's rows stay on the GPU, parked once with one output stream per destination'; engine.rs run_fragment_inner relays parked batches only after build(). FE deploys root-first (ExecutionDAG.getFragmentsInTopologicalOrderFromRoot), so every leaf of a query runs in one wave and each parks its full output before any receiver starts.
3. The pool was exactly full at every OOM. Engine log window for q05 (cn1/engine-.cn0.log lines 49010-62106): 5005 OOM lines, every one 'global usage 107374182400 bytes (102400.00 MB)' = 100 GiB; gpu_pool QueryEnd peak=107374182400. The retry count per query is an exact multiple of 100 equal to (scan tasks not yet parked) x 100: q05 40 parked batches (104.3 GB) + 25 pending x 100 = 2500; q17 25 + 21x100 = 2100; q18 14 + 23x100 = 2300; q21 10 + 18x100 = 1800. Every pending scan task exhausted its budget; none ever succeeded after the pool filled.
4. The retry loop really cannot free the memory, and the code says why. The 1-CN derived config (experimental/starrocks/.cn0/derived-sirius-config.yaml) has gpu usage_limit_bytes 100GiB AND host capacity_bytes 160GiB, and gpu_pipeline_executor.cpp ~:197-215 does call request_downgrade on a partial reservation. But the q05 window shows 2503 x '[downgrade] request not satisfied and disk memory space is not configured' and per task 'after downgrade (0 bytes freed), reservation still partial (3318948864/5803790251 bytes) -- proceeding with partial'; host_pool peak stayed at 33.99 GB all session. Reason: downgrade_executor.cpp:223-233 sweeps only repositories reachable through _data_repo_registry (the per-query data_repository_manager), while the parked sender output repositories are created in streaming_fragment.cpp:103-112 as standalone make_shared<shared_data_repository>() that 'escape data_repository_manager_ cleanup so sender output outlives this fragment'. Parked batches are idle with zero subscribers (they would pass convertible_data_batch.hpp try_get_batch) but they are never enumerated. So the '100 GiB pool' framing is correct in effect even though a 160 GiB host tier exists.
5. MAX_RETRIES=100 / 50 ms is a compile-time constant (gpu_pipeline_executor.cpp:348-372); no env or yaml knob. No CN env knob fuses fragments (full list: SIRIUS_BUILD_DIR, SIRIUS_CN_ASYNC_SENDER_DISPATCH, SIRIUS_CN_DUMP_FRAGMENTS, SIRIUS_CN_TRANSLATE_ONLY, SIRIUS_CN_USE_SIRIUS_DATASOURCE, SIRIUS_DUCKDB_PARQUET_EXTENSION, SIRIUS_EXCHANGE_STAGING_BYTES, SIRIUS_LOG_DIR, SIRIUS_SUBSTRAIT_PLAN). FE: CostModel.java:419-441 prices BROADCAST at outputSize x aliveBackendNumber and SHUFFLE at outputSize x factor; with cardinality 1 (StatisticsCalculator.computeFileScanNode:664-677) the choice is a tie-break, and broadcast_row_limit never fires. The only existing path to keep lineitem local is a per-query SQL hint (JOIN [BROADCAST] with lineitem as the left operand, plus disable_join_reorder) — a workaround, not a knob.
6. Standalone contrast confirmed: standalone-failed/runs/q05.explain.txt has READ_PARQUET lineitem (~6.11e9) as the left/probe child of HASH_JOIN l_orderkey=o_orderkey with the ~61.6M-row orders chain as build; q18 likewise probes lineitem; q17/q21 use DELIM joins; runs.csv warm 2786/3674/5427/3786/2691/6401 ms, all MATCH vs the oracle.

result.reasoning:
Partial verdict: the leak MECHANISM and every leak NUMBER in OOM-5 reproduce, but the headline causal clause ("directly caused q17 to die with only 66 GB of its own data parked") and the impact clause ("shrinking the headroom that decides pass/fail") are contradicted by the measurements, so the finding as written is refuted and should be kept only in the corrected, downgraded form below.

CONFIRMED (measured): (1) Code: experimental/starrocks/src/compute_node_service.rs:449-478 cancel_plan_fragment only calls results.cancel() and its doc comment says engine abort / parked-state teardown is "a separate work item"; run_ready_fragment (:862-905) on a receiver failure only calls results.fail_query(); engine.rs:278-300 serves Run requests one at a time and clears parked/parked_slots only when run_fragment returns Err. (2) cn1/cluster.log (ANSI-stripped to agent-notes/refute-oom5/cn-events.txt): after each `fragment run failed`, the dead query's not-yet-run senders still start and finish: q05 lines 6072-6305 (..5773, ..5777, ..5776, ..5775 with inputs=2 draining streams 1/4), q08 9513-9616, q09 12001-12206 (..947 ..946 ..945 ..944), q17 17806-17984 (two senders, one 6343 ms), q21 21467-21609 (one drains stream 6 = 730,806,711 rows, 3153 ms); q18 had none left. (3) engine-cn0.log pool trace (agent-notes/refute-oom5/pool-trace.txt) reproduces every cited value: 104.30->0.00->4.69 (q05); 104.24->0.00->8.78/8.83 (q08); 105.24 @13:12:22.323 ->0.00 @22.333 ->0.08->13.18->31.56 @22.714 (q09), baseline 31.56 GB at every QueryBegin of q10..q16; q16 partsupp sender q=649 31.56->38.16 (dump fragment-0421 confirms partsupp); q17 lineitem sender q=653 Begin 38.16 @13:13:13.067, End 104.42 @13:14:56.804 (66.26 GB); q17 leftover leaks 4.00 GB into q18; q18 failure leaks 0 (q19 begins at 0.00); q21 failure leaks 36.64 GB into q22 (not cited by the analyst).

REFUTED (causal/impact): q17's lineitem sender (dump cn1/dump/fragment-0427.txt: FILE_SCAN lineitem, 32 scan ranges, no filter) parked 25 batches = 66.26 GB (cn1-quent.txt q17.r0 STREAMING_SINK in=66.26GB) = 2.65 GB/batch, with 21 more tasks stuck (analyst's own count, 46 total). The identical projection in standalone is GPU_SCAN(3) n=46 in=122.25 GB (agent-notes/standalone-failed-quent.txt q17.r0 and r1). 122 GB > the 107.37 GB pool cap, so the sender cannot be parked even in a clean pool; the 38.16 GB leak only moved the death from ~40 batches to 25 batches. The same holds for every other failure (analyst's table in oom-failures.md section 2): q05 171.0 GB, q08 195.75, q09 244.5, q18 97.5 + 64.7 GB of its own other senders, q21 123.0 + 77.76 own. No failure in this campaign is attributable to the leak, and no pass/fail flipped: all 15 passing queries passed while carrying 4.69 (q06, q07), 31.56 (q10-q15) or 36.64 GB (q22) of leaked baseline (agent-notes/refute-oom5/headroom.txt). The cn4 arm had 0 failures and 0 wipes, so it neither confirms nor contradicts.

The claim should be re-stated as: a real, six-for-six reproducible leak of 0-36.6 GB per failure plus 0.4-6.4 s of engine-thread time stolen from the next query, with an order-dependence RISK (inference: q07's boundary-sampled own peak 79.17 GB + 31.56 GB = 110.7 GB > 107.37 would have OOMed if scheduled between q09 and q17) but no measured effect on any pass/fail result at SF1000. The proposed change (per-query parked drop + skip pending Runs of a failed query + cancel drops parked state) remains well-motivated; its confidence as a fix for the six OOM failures is nil, its confidence as a hygiene/latency fix is high.

result.reasoning:
Re-derived every cited number from the evidence bundle and found no contradiction that breaks the causal chain; the finding stands with attribution corrections.

MEASURED FACTS THAT REPRODUCE
1. Timings (runs.csv): cn1 q02 1707/1264/1227 ms; cn4 2158/1264/1044 ms; standalone 816/568/574 ms. Warm medians 1245/1154/571 -> 2.18x (per run 2.14-2.23x) and 1.08x. results.md and results-ratios.md agree.
2. FE plan (survey/explain/q02.costs.txt): join 4 INNER JOIN (BROADCAST) build = 3:EXCHANGE (lines 519-535, inside PLAN FRAGMENT 11(F00) at 500-558 whose OutPut Exchange Id is 06); join 31 PARTITIONED, exch 28 partition exprs n_regionkey, exch 30 r_regionkey (305-327); join 37 BROADCAST build = exch 36 with filter_id 7 build_expr ps_partkey remote=true (73-97); fragment F11 (343-420) is partsupp FileScanNode 19 -> join 22 (supplier broadcast exch 21) -> join 26 (nation broadcast exch 25) -> shuffle 28. The 4-CN plan (survey/explain4/q02.costs.txt) has exch 4 on ps_partkey (line 557), 21 on ps_suppkey (438), 26 on s_nationkey (381), 31 on n_regionkey (326), join 5 PARTITIONED build = exch 4 partsupp (541-558).
3. Actual rows (card-compare, derived by card_compare.py from run 0's 'declared input stream cardinality', summed over CNs): cn1 exch 3 = 800,000,000, exch 28 = 800,000,000, exch 34/36 = 118,065,576, exch 6 = 3,191,000, exch 25 = 25, exch 30 = 1; cn4 exch 4/21/26/31 = 800,000,000 each, exch 39 = 472,262,304 = 4 x 118,065,576 exactly, exch 2 = 797,750. cn1-cnlog.txt confirms identical declared cards in all three runs.
4. Engine behaviour inside F00 (cn1-quent.txt:118-122 and cn1-ops.txt block for ...f56c): pipeline [GPU_SCAN(0) part 4.45 GB -> PARTITION(1) 0.02 GB -> CONCAT(2) 0.02 GB] is the build; pipeline [STREAMING_SOURCE(3) -> DYNAMIC_FILTER(4)] takes the 13.10 GB partsupp stream and emits 0.05 GB into PARTITION(5)/CONCAT(6); HASH_JOIN(7) input 0.07 GB. So the engine did build on part and probe with a join-filtered partsupp; the FE's broadcast build side was overridden in-fragment, but the 13.1 GB stream was still fully scanned (fragment ...f56d GPU_SCAN 0.788 s, 5 tasks) and parked (F00 wall 0.707 s vs Comp 0.219 s, dwell_max 0.648 s).
5. Subquery chain (cn1-quent.txt:134-138, cn1-ops block for ...f566): GPU_SCAN(6) 0.779 s 13.10 GB, HASH_JOIN(10) 0.289 s input 13.18 GB, HASH_JOIN(14) 0.399 s input 13.00 GB, no dynamic filter, wall 0.438 s of a 1.063 s span (41.2%). F19 (...f564): HASH_JOIN(7) 0.243 s over 13.00 GB + HASH_GROUP_BY 0.064 + MERGE_GROUP_BY 0.019 s.
6. Standalone (standalone-quent.txt:24-29, r1): Comp 1.826 s, GPU_SCAN 0.765+0.757+0.203+0.044 = 1.769 s, everything else 0.057 s; standalone/runs/q02.explain.txt shows LEFT_DELIM_JOIN on p_partkey with READ_PARQUET part (filters suffix BRASS, p_size=15) as build of the main join and DELIM_SCAN feeding the subquery's partsupp join. reservation-ratio.txt:4,19,34: Comp cn1 2.9 s, cn4 4.6 s, standalone 1.8 s. Both arms scan partsupp twice (2 x 13.10 GB) at the same cost (~1.55-1.57 s); the CN's ~1.0 s excess Computing is entirely the joins/aggs over 800M rows in F11/F19.
7. 4 CN: cn4-transmits.txt:6-8 = 135 transmits, 45.14/43.60/45.66 GB; cn4-quent.txt:316 q02.r1 span 1.077 s leases 402 / 108.08 GB / 41.351 s.
8. Sources: StatisticsCalculator.java:664-674 setOutputRowCount(1) + ColumnStatistic.unknown(); HashJoinCostModel.java:140-142 mapSize from rightStatistics.getOutputRowCount(); EnforceAndCostTask.java:281-320 checkBroadcastRowCountLimit reads the (=1) statistics. grep 'runtime_filter|runtimefilter|runtime filter' over crates/starrocks-plan-translator/src and experimental/starrocks/src = 1 hit (wire_type_parity.rs:607 test fixture). The FE does ship the filters: cn1/dump/fragment-0022.txt:644-904 has build_runtime_filters: Some(TRuntimeFilterDescription{... runtime_filter_merge_nodes ...}) and build_runtime_filters_from_planner, and the plan attaches probe filters to the scans (q02.costs.txt F14 nation scan: filter_id 6 probe_expr n_regionkey; F01 partsupp scan: filters 1, 7, 8; F00 part scan: 0, 7). Measured non-application: exch 25 carried 25 nation rows (card-compare-cn1.txt:11), not the 5 European ones filter 6 would leave, so exch 28 carried 800M rows instead of ~160M.

WHY NOT REFUTED
The chain 'cardinality 1 -> FE puts partsupp on build/shuffle paths and never pushes the p_partkey correlation into the subquery -> 800M rows through three joins + aggregation -> ~1.0 s extra Computing and a longer rendezvous chain -> 2.2x behind standalone; on 4 CNs the FE re-plans into 4 x 800M shuffles + 4 x 118M broadcast with no span reduction' is supported at every link by measured data. No other query or arm contradicts it: the scan-heavy queries with the same cardinality-1 defect reach parity because the in-fragment DuckDB re-plan neutralizes the build-side choice (q04 3.79B build, parity 0.98; q07 1.5B build, parity 1.06), which is exactly what q02's F00 also shows; q02 is worse because the subquery decorrelation is a fragment-cut decision the engine cannot undo. Run-to-run consistency: cn1 and standalone are within 3%; cn4 has a 21% spread (see corrections), but even the best 4-CN run gives only 1.19x wall / 1.24x span.

The finding's weaknesses are attribution and wording (below), not evidence gaps.
result.corrections:
1. 'on 4 CNs the same plan shuffles partsupp four times' -- not the same plan. With 4 alive CNs the FE produces 16 fragments instead of 13 (survey/plan-summary-4cn.txt vs plan-summary.txt): join 4 BROADCAST becomes join 5 PARTITIONED, the part side is shuffled too (exch 2 = 797,750 rows), and the subquery chain becomes three PARTITIONED joins (24/29/34). The four 800M-row shuffles (exch 4, 21, 26, 31) and their keys are correctly listed; two of them (26, 31) carry joined intermediates, not raw partsupp.
2. 'broadcasts 472M rows' -- exch 39 = 118,065,576 rows x 4 receivers (card_compare sums declared rows over CNs). State it as a 118M-row table delivered to 4 CNs.
3. 'gains only 1.08x' -- median of n=2 with a 21% spread on 4 CN (1264 vs 1044 ms; cn1 1264/1227). Per-run wall speed-up 0.97-1.19x, engine span 0.99-1.24x (cn4 spans 1.077/0.832 s vs cn1 1.063/1.031 s); cold run is slower on 4 CN (2158 vs 1707 ms). 'Does not scale' is robust, the digit is not.
4. Lease numbers: q02.r1 (402 leases / 108.08 GB / 41.35 s held) is the high run; r0 = 384 / 91.92 GB / 58.9 s and r2 = 238 / 70.80 GB / 11.77 s (cn4-quent.txt:115,316,517) with identical nixl volume (43.6-45.7 GB) and identical declared cardinalities. lease_GB is 1.6-2.4x the nixl bytes and quent_bp.py attributes leases by time window (lines 102-106), so it is not a per-query transfer volume; quote the nixl bytes for volume and the lease range for pressure. 'inside a 1.08 s query' is the Quent span; the client wall for that run was 1264 ms.
5. 'wall 443 ms = 41% of the 1067 ms span' -- cn1-quent.txt:103,134 give 438 ms of a 1.063 s span (41.2%); 443 ms is the cnlog slowest-sender figure for that run.
6. Attribution of the 1-CN vs standalone gap: the build-side placement of partsupp in join 4 is neutralized inside F00 (part build 0.02 GB, DYNAMIC_FILTER 13.10 -> 0.05 GB, HASH_JOIN(7) 0.07 GB) at a cost of only the parked scan (F01 GPU_SCAN 0.788 s, identical to standalone's GPU_SCAN(37) 0.757 s). The ~1.0 s of excess Computing is the missing correlation pushdown: F11 joins 0.69 s + F19 join/aggs 0.33 s over 800M rows versus <0.06 s of non-scan work in the standalone DELIM plan. Lead with the subquery chain, not the build side. Additionally ~200 ms of the 696 ms gap lies outside the engine span (wall - span: cn1 201/196 ms, cn4 187/212 ms, standalone 22/21 ms), i.e. FE planning/dispatch/result path, not plan shape.
7. Runtime-filter nuance: in the current plan the FE's remote filters mostly run the unhelpful direction. Filter 7 (min-table ps_partkey -> main part/partsupp scans) would prune ~41% (118M of 200M part keys survive); filter 8 (min values -> ps_supplycost) prunes ~nothing; filter 1/4/5 carry all suppliers/nations. The one that matters, filter 6 (r_regionkey -> F14 nation scan), measurably did not apply (exch 25 = 25 rows), so exch 28 / join 31 processed 800M rows instead of ~160M -- worth about 0.25 s of the 1.0 s excess. The 'part filter -> subquery partsupp' filter the proposal relies on does not exist in this plan; it requires the CBO to flip join 37's build side (needs a cardinality/NDV estimate for the aggregate output vs the ~640K-row main chain), which parquet footers do not supply (no NDV) -- the FE change confidence should be lower than 'medium-high' for that specific effect.

result.corrections:
1. "the lineitem sender fragment itself cannot fit its own output in the 100 GiB pool" is true for q05 (171 GB), q08 (196 GB), q09 (245 GB), q17 (122 GB) and q21's unfiltered l2 sender (~117 GB = 46 x 2.54 GB), but NOT for q18: its full lineitem projection is 97.5 GB (37 x 2.56 GB) < 107.37 GB pool. q18 died because 64.7 GB of other exchange inputs were already parked (cn1-quent.txt:1081-1100: customer ...ad9a 3.94 GB, aggregate fragment ...ad9d ~24 GB, orders ...ad9e 36.75 GB) when the lineitem sender ...ad9c started. q21 likewise had 77.76 GB parked by the filtered sender (cn1-quent.txt:1252-1256, fragment-0502 -> exchange 2) before the failing sender began. The accurate statement is: the SUM of concurrently parked exchange inputs of one query (plus post-failure leftovers of earlier queries, oom-failures.md section 3/6) exceeds the pool, and nothing can be spilled.

2. q21 attribution: the OOM'd sender (instance ...2aca) is cn1/dump/fragment-0504.txt: FILE_SCAN node 12 -> dest_node_id 13, i.e. the build of 14:LEFT SEMI JOIN (BUCKET_SHUFFLE(S)) (the unfiltered EXISTS l2 scan), not the 10:RIGHT ANTI JOIN exchanges named in the claim. Exchange 9 is fed by fragment-0503/0507 (PROJECT 8, HASH_JOIN 7, FILE_SCAN 3 lineitem, EXCHANGE 6 = broadcast orders 730.8M rows; that lineitem scan stays inside the join fragment) and exchange 2 by fragment-0502 (filtered l3, 77.76 GB parked). Also the claim's q21 tally "46 tasks" vs "10 parked + 18 stuck = 28" is not a match: the query died once the first original task hit 100 retries; 18 of the 46 tasks never ran.

3. Impact "unrunnable ... regardless of CN count" is inference, not measurement: cn4/runs/runs.csv contains no rows for q05/q08/q09/q17/q18/q21 (the 4-CN arm skipped them). The FE splits FILES() scan ranges across CNs (FileScanNode.java:542-548: numInstances = min(totalBytes/64 MB, nodes x parallelInstanceNum); :552-600 assigns files to the least-loaded location), and the 4-CN Quent confirms a 4-way split (cn4-quent.txt q04.r1: the four orders senders each GPU_SCAN in=24.4-24.8 GB of the ~98 GB table). So at 4 CNs the per-CN parked lineitem projection would be ~43/49/61/31/24/31 GB, which fits a 107 GiB pool; if these queries still fail at 4 CNs it would be in the receiver's hash build (1.5B lineitem rows per CN as build side), a different mechanism that was not measured. The 4-CN plan is also not identical: q21's 10:RIGHT ANTI JOIN becomes BUCKET_SHUFFLE(S) with a co-located scan (plan-summary-4cn.txt), and q05/q08/q09 flip several BROADCAST joins to PARTITIONED. Corroboration exists only at 2 CNs with smaller pools: benchmarks/pinned/README.md:140-144 records the same six OOMing on 2x RTX PRO 6000 (96 GiB, SF500 budgets) and explicitly expects larger HBM to clear some.

4. "parquet footer row counts fetched with the schema": PGetFileSchemaResult (gensrc/proto/internal_service.proto:647-650) carries only status + schema, so this path needs a proto change plus a CN change in experimental/starrocks/src/file_schema.rs (which already opens the parquet footer). The byte-size path needs no wire change: TableFunctionTable.java:188 holds fileStatuses (TBrokerFileStatus.size), loadFileList() is public (:300), and FileScanNode.java:535-539 already sums totalBytes; LogicalScanOperator.getTable() (:110) exposes the table from computeFileScanNode. Likewise a CN-side byte threshold does not need footers: every TBrokerRangeDesc in the fragment already carries file_size (fragment-0141.txt:4796, e.g. 2,953,165,132 B).

5. Feasibility risk of the FE fix on 1 CN (inference from cost code, medium confidence): CostModel.java:419-426 multiplies a BROADCAST exchange's cost by BROADCAST_JOIN_MEM_EXCEED_PENALTY = 1000 (StatisticsEstimateCoefficient.java:60) when the broadcast side's outputSize exceeds exec_mem_limit (DEFAULT_EXEC_MEM_LIMIT 2 GiB, SessionVariable.java:1305), while SHUFFLE network cost is 0 on a single node (CostModel.java:432-441 with enable_local_shuffle_agg=true, enable_pipeline=true, SystemInfoService.isSingleBackendAndComputeNode). With real statistics the small side of lineitem's join is orders-derived (q18 ~308M rows, q05 227M filtered orders -> tens of GB), so broadcast would still lose to a free shuffle at 1 CN and lineitem would still cross an exchange unless exec_mem_limit is raised or the penalty is changed. broadcast_row_limit (15M) is not the blocker: EnforceAndCostTask.java:324-327 only applies it when leftOutputSize < rightOutputSize x beNum x 10. The actual CBO outcome needs an EXPLAIN with statistics, which was not run.

6. Existing knobs the finding should mention: SQL join hints `[BROADCAST]` are honored (JoinHelper.java:344-348 onlyBroadcast on HintNode.HINT_JOIN_BROADCAST; RequiredPropertyDeriver.java:141-149 then offers only the broadcast property; EnforceAndCostTask.java:291-296 zeroes the hinted child's cost) and would keep lineitem in its scan fragment without FE code changes (a query rewrite, but a valid test of the hypothesis). exec_mem_limit and broadcast_row_limit are session variables. On the CN/engine side there is no knob: MAX_RETRIES is a constexpr and the only SIRIUS_CN_* tunables (tunable.rs/engine_settings.rs) are nixl/RPC/Quent settings. A refusal precedent exists in compute_node_service.rs:1063-1071 (unsupported sinks refused by name) and the CN receives all of its fragments in one exec_batch_plan_fragments call (:424-447), so a sender-plus-receiver shape check is feasible where proposed.

"never materialises it" is right in substance but overstated: DuckDB's plan still materialises lineitem-derived aggregate state in q18 (HASH_GROUP_BY over 5.999B rows -> ~1.5B groups; standalone-failed-quent HASH_GROUP_BY(4) in=97.50 GB) and q17 (DELIM aggregate), but those are far smaller than the raw projection, and the full-width lineitem is always the probe side.

result.reasoning:
The plan-level facts in PC-3 hold, but the causal claim ("This is the measured source of ... the 0.43-0.59 scaling efficiency") and several of its example attributions are contradicted by the measurements.

WHAT SURVIVES (measured):
- Distribution decisions and row counts: card-compare-cn4.txt lines for q03 exch2=3,234,397,656 (SHUFFLE) vs exch9=145,769,513 (build of 10:INNER JOIN PARTITIONED); q12 exch1=1.5B vs exch4=31,162,904; q10 exch8=1,480,675,200 vs exch11=57,358,391; q19 exch4=128,557,109 vs exch1=2,158,428; q22 exch10=6.0B BROADCAST; q07 exch17=600M; q02 exch39=472,262,304. Re-derived from cn4-cnlog.json declared_cardinalities: identical in r0/r1/r2 for every stream of every cited query (4 receivers each), so the numbers are stable.
- Cost model: CostModel.java visitPhysicalDistribution: BROADCAST = CostEstimate.of(outputSize*aliveBackendNumber, outputSize*beNum, max(outputSize*beNum,1)); SHUFFLE = CostEstimate.of(outputSize*factor, 0, max(outputSize,1)*factor). With cardinality 1 everywhere the flip is CN-count arithmetic, as claimed. EnforceAndCostTask.checkBroadcastRowCountLimit returns false when broadcast_row_limit<=0 (SessionVariable.java:465 BROADCAST_ROW_LIMIT), hint parsing at AstBuilder.java:6567 — code refs check out.
- The mechanism is real and on the critical path for q03 and q10 only: cn4-quent.json q03.r1 lineitem sender fragment wall 1.283 s vs Computing/4 = 0.588 s (gap +0.695 s) while every no-exchange scan fragment has a gap of +0.03..+0.15 s (q06 +0.06, q01 +0.14, q12 lineitem +0.11, q19 +0.15, q04 +0.13); the q03 join fragment starts at +1.280 s exactly when the sender ends. q10.r1: lineitem sender wall 1.125-1.264 vs 0.48 (gap +0.64), customer sender (stream 5, 19.15 GB, 150M rows with string columns) wall 1.337 vs Comp 0.684. q22: HASH_JOIN(15) 0.516 s per CN on the broadcast 1.5B-row anti-join build inside a 0.685 s span.

CONTRADICTIONS:
1. The efficiency band exists without any movement. results-ratios.md + cn4-transmits.txt: q01 0.00 GB moved -> efficiency 0.59; q06 0.00 GB -> 0.56; q15 1.27 GB -> 0.58; q19 2.75 GB -> 0.53; q14 5.43 GB -> 0.53. Heavy movers: q03 60.34 GB -> 0.48, q10 48.04 GB -> 0.52, q07 69.01 GB -> 0.43. Movement therefore accounts for at most ~0.05-0.15 of efficiency for the heaviest queries and none of the ~0.4 baseline loss.
2. The baseline loss is measured elsewhere. (a) GPU_SCAN Computing seconds per input GB (Quent top_ops, cn1-quent.json vs cn4-quent.json, r1) rise 1.3-1.6x on 4 CNs for every query regardless of movement: q01 0.047->0.072, q06 0.067->0.096, q19 0.046->0.065, q14 0.069->0.112, q12 0.040->0.055, q03 0.045->0.063, q04 0.042->0.059, q10 0.041->0.051, q07 0.049->0.071, q15 0.066->0.101, q20 0.080->0.137. The scan-heavy fragments are compute-bound on the 4 pipeline threads (wall ~= Computing/4 on both arms), so per-CN scan work is 1/4 x 1.3-1.6 = 0.33-0.40 of 1-CN, capping the engine-span speed-up at ~2.5-3x before anything else. (Cause of the per-GB slowdown - shared host/storage read path with 4 concurrent CNs - is inference.) (b) Non-engine overhead (runs.csv client ms minus Quent span) is ~0.18-0.28 s per run on BOTH arms: cn4 q06.r1 853-675=178, q03.r1 1639-1418=221, q01.r1 2022-1779=243, q12.r1 1304-1073=231, q07.r1 2022-1790=232, q10.r1 1751-1474=277; cn1 q06.r1 1909-1701=208, q03.r1 3031-2794=237, q01.r1 5190-4946=244. On engine span alone q01 reaches 2.78x (0.70) and q06 2.52x (0.63). (c) Staggered fragment starts: q07.r1 lineitem scan starts at +0.304 s of a 1.790 s span; q12.r1 lineitem at +0.22 s of 1.073; q10.r1 cn2 lineitem at +0.371 vs +0.014-0.020 on the other CNs.
3. q12 is a counter-example to its own listing: the 1.5B-row orders shuffle fragment computes 0.255 s (GPU_SCAN 0.163 + STREAMING_SINK 0.093) and overlaps the compute-bound lineitem scan (wall 0.737 vs Comp/4 0.66); its wall of 0.974 s is rendezvous waiting, and the join starts at +0.956. q12's loss is scan-rate + late start + client overhead, not the shuffle.
4. q07 attribution is wrong: the cited "wrong broadcast" (exch17 customer) carries 3.71 GB of q07's 69.01 GB (stream-level transmit bytes in cn4-cnlog.json). The dominant q07 movement is exch8 = 1,822,871,264 lineitem rows shuffled as the BUILD side of 9:INNER JOIN (PARTITIONED) against a 799,746-row supplier probe (43.75 GB) plus exch13 orders 1.5B (13.50 GB) - the biggest single mis-cut in the campaign after q03, and it is absent from the claim. q07's lineitem sender gap is +0.30 s on 4 CN vs +0.44 s on 1 CN, so movement is not q07's dominant loss either.
5. q02 attribution is wrong: exch39 (472M rows) moves 4.25 GB of 43.6-45.7 GB; the four 800M-row partsupp shuffles (streams 4, 21, 26, 31 = 9.6 GB each, 38.5 GB) dominate because the FE joins partsupp->supplier->nation->region with the EUROPE filter last and reshuffles the 800M-row intermediate three times (plan-summary-4cn.txt q02 joins 5/24/29/34). That is a join-order problem, not a broadcast one.
6. q19's 128.6M-row lineitem shuffle moves only 2.70 GB, per-sender transmit sum ~60 ms, sender gap +0.15 s (= no-exchange baseline); it has no measurable cost and its efficiency (0.53) equals q01/q06's.
7. "the joins that stay BROADCAST are the wrong ones": 11 of 27 broadcast joins survive on 4 CN (16 flip, 59% - not "almost every"; q20 and q22 plans are unchanged). Only 3 survivors are oversize (q22 orders 18.56 GB, q07 customer 3.71 GB, q02 exch39 4.25 GB); q03 exch6 (customer 30M x4 = 0.37 GB), q10 exch2 nation, q11 exch7/20 (400K x4), q20 exch21 (3.3M x4), q02 exch13/17 are right-sized broadcasts.
8. Wire time is small: per-sender summed nixl elapsed per run <= 0.30 s (q03), 0.35 s (q07), 0.26 s (q10), 0.14 s (q12), 0.085 s (q22); write_ms sums 24-79 ms; lease-wait sums <= 27 ms (cn4-cnlog.json transmits). The q03/q10 stall is parked output/held leases, not transfer - the analyst's "staging-lease time it induces" is consistent but remains inference.

Verdict: the planning observations and per-exchange numbers are correct and reproducible, but the finding overstates the flip, misattributes q07/q02/q19, and its headline causal claim about the 0.43-0.59 efficiency is contradicted by zero-movement queries in the same band and by the measured per-GB scan slowdown plus fixed overheads that account for the bulk of the loss.

result.reasoning:
MECHANISM: CONFIRMED from source. (1) compute_node_service.rs:449-476 `cancel_plan_fragment` does exactly one thing besides logging: `self.core.results.cancel(id, reason)`, and result_store.rs:205-213 `cancel` only flips a still-Waiting result entry to Failed. It never touches LocalExchange, the dispatch queue or the engine thread; the docstring itself says "Real teardown (aborting the engine run, freeing GPU buffers, dropping parked exchange state) is a separate work item." (2) engine.rs:267-275 declares `parked`/`parked_slots`/`poisoned` with no query_id bookkeeping (ExecuteRequest carries `label.query_id`, engine.rs ~70, but it is not stored in ParkedOutput); engine.rs:291-316 is the only wipe and fires only when `run_fragment` returns Err, clearing every slot. Local parked outputs are otherwise released only by `relay_from`+`release_slot` inside a receiver run (engine.rs ~595-612). `DropParked` exists (engine.rs:99-105, trait `drop_parked` fragment_executor.rs:220) but is called only from nixl_transport.rs:412 and :790 for remote drains. (3) `try_dispatch_sender` (compute_node_service.rs:309-330) queues every sender-only fragment at arrival onto the single `dispatch_worker` (:380-391), which pops sequentially and never consults query state; `run_ready_fragment` (:864-905) on Err calls `results.fail_query` (result_store.rs:163-200), which records `query_failures` (:98), but that map is read only by `reserve()` (:127) — no sender/Run path checks it. (4) LocalExchange removes receivers/sources only in `take_ready` (local_exchange.rs:284-308); pending receivers of a dead query and their LocalParked SenderSlots stay forever. In `execute_ready_fragment` (compute_node_service.rs:1325-1400) a translation failure (the q16 case) returns Err while holding the LocalParked slots, without `drop_parked` — so the q16 claim ("never reached the engine thread") is exactly right. (5) FE side: DefaultCoordinator.java:1085-1107 `cancelInternal` -> :1161 `cancelRemoteFragmentsAsync` cancels every unfinished instance (cluster.log:16607 "has unfinished instances: [...]"), matching the 11/9/5 cancel acks seen. (6) No knob covers it: SIRIUS_CN_ASYNC_SENDER_DISPATCH (compute_node_service.rs:271-299) off only moves the queue from the dispatch worker to the engine request channel (engine_call blocks per RPC thread); queued Runs still execute after a sibling's Err.

LOGS/NUMBERS: all verified. q05: cluster.log:6050 (wipe slots=2) then 6072/6181/6258/6291 senders 5773, 5777, 5776 and middle fragment 5775 (inputs=2) run after the 13:05:24.627 failure; engine-cn0.log lines 61744-61883: 0 -> 0.08 -> 1.32 -> 4.11 -> 4.69 GB, q06/q07 begin at 4.69 GB. q08: lines 82268-82438: 0 -> 0.08 -> 7.54 -> 8.78 GB; q09 begins 8.83 GB, End 105.24 GB (110473). q09: wipe slots=7 (cluster.log:11962), 110479-110569: 0 -> 0.08 -> 13.18 -> 31.56 GB (= 947 supplier 0.08 + 946 partsupp 13.10 + 945 orders 18.38 per cn1-quent.txt:557-575), baseline 31.56-31.80 GB at every boundary through 13:13:12.548; q16 ff87 adds 6.6 GB -> 38.16 GB (117084-117102); q17 eaca3 Begin 38.16 GB (117132) -> End 104.42 GB (127667) = 38.16 + 66.26.

REFUTED PART OF THE CLAIM: "directly caused q17 to die with only 66 GB of its own data parked" is arithmetically false. q17 PLAN FRAGMENT 4(F00) (survey/explain/q17.costs.txt) is a bare lineitem FileScanNode -> EXCHANGE 01 shuffle with output l_partkey INT, l_quantity, l_extendedprice; the FE's runtime filters (filter_id 0/1 on l_partkey) are not implemented by the translator (grep runtime_filter in crates/starrocks-plan-translator/src: nothing), so the whole table must be parked (fact 2: nothing streams across a fragment boundary). lineitem SF1000 = 5,999,989,709 rows (parquet metadata; 60 files, 5640 row groups); parked row = 4 + 8 + 8 = 20 B (decimals are lowered to 8-byte values; calibrated on q07: fragment 0c2a 1,822,871,264 rows -> 59.47 GB = 32.6 B/row for i64+i32+3x8B, and 0c29 1.5B rows -> 18.38 GB = 12.25 B/row for i64+i32). F00 alone therefore needs >= 120 GB in a 107.37 GB (100 GiB) pool: q17 cannot complete with zero leak. The leak only moved the death point (25 of ~2.6 GB sink batches parked instead of ~40). The same holds for every other failure: q05 F06 (l_orderkey, l_suppkey, l_extendedprice, l_discount) >= 28 B x 6.0B = 168 GB and it was the FIRST failure (no leak in; parked 104.30 GB at death); q08 F02 >= 32 B -> 192 GB; q09 F02 >= 40 B -> 240 GB; q18 F04 16 B -> 96 GB plus its own siblings 3.94 + 24.0 + 36.75 = 64.7 GB parked = 161 GB; q21 started with ZERO leak (q19/q20 ended at allocated=0, engine 139656/140230) and died at 103.14 GB = 77.76 GB (filtered l1 PROJECTION sink) + 25.37 GB (F08 partial), all its own, while F08 needs 12 B x 6.0B = 72 GB -> 150 GB. No pass/fail in this campaign was decided by the leak, and every passing run that executed under a leak shows oom_resched=0 in cn1-cnlog.txt (q06/q07 under 4.69 GB, q10-q15 under 31.6-38.2 GB, q22 under 5.94 GB); engine-cn0.log has 0 "OOM at operator" lines between 13:12:22.333 and 13:13:13.060 (the q10-q16 window).

WHY refuted=false: the code does what the finding says, the proposed change is feasible where proposed, and nothing existing covers it; the error is in the causal/impact attribution, which is a correction, not a code-level contradiction of the mechanism. The order-dependence risk is real in principle: q07's own parked footprint is 79.2 GB (59.47 + 18.38 + 1.24 + 0.08; engine allocated 83.86 GB at 13:05:34.098, line 62303, with 4.69 GB leaked), so under the 38.16 GB leak q07 would need ~117 GB > 107 GB and would have failed had it run after q09/q16 — inference, not observed.

FEASIBILITY of the proposed change: (a) store `request.label.query_id` next to ParkedOutput at park time (engine.rs park block ~626-643) and on Err drop only that query's park ids — small, local, no FE cooperation. (b) skip queued Runs of a failed query: the record already exists (ResultStore.query_failures, result_store.rs:98) but has no accessor and is never consulted on the sender path; add one and check it in run_ready_fragment/dispatch_worker, or keep a failed-query set on the engine thread. Note the race the logs show: the dispatch worker popped 5773 at 13:05:24.632012, before the FE's first cancel ack at .632266 (cluster.log:6072-6073), so cancel-driven cleanup alone misses the first leftover; Err-time bookkeeping is the robust variant. (c) cancel-driven drop needs a LocalExchange method to remove pending receivers/sources by query (none exists; removals only in take_ready) and then DropParked per slot; the cheap immediate fix for the q16 pattern is to `drop_parked` the LocalParked slots in run_ready_fragment's Err arm when translation fails before the run (the slots are already in hand in ReadyFragment.inputs).

result.reasoning:
The measured core of PC-3 holds up against the source and the evidence: (1) the FE plan shape really does change with the CN count at cardinality 1 (survey/plan-summary.txt vs plan-summary-4cn.txt: q03 orders join BROADCAST->PARTITIONED, q12/q19 lineitem build BROADCAST->PARTITIONED, q02 13->16 fragments; q22 anti join and q07 customer join stay BROADCAST); (2) the row counts quoted are exactly what card-compare-cn4.txt records (q03 exch2 3,234,397,656 vs exch9 145,769,513; q12 exch1 1.5B vs exch4 31,162,904; q10 exch8 1,480,675,200 vs exch11 57,358,391; q19 exch4 128,557,109 vs exch1 2,158,428; q22 exch10 6.0B; q07 exch17 600M; q02 exch39 472M); (3) the nixl bytes are consistent with those rows: the CN routes a destination whose brpc address matches its own identity as DestinationRoute::Local (compute_node_service.rs:1251-1274), so a 4-way shuffle moves 3/4 of the rows and a broadcast 3 copies; q03: 3.234B x 24 B (l_orderkey BIGINT + l_extendedprice + l_discount DECIMAL64, FE PrimitiveType.getTypeSize 8 each) x 0.75 = 58.2 GB + 146M x 16 B x 0.75 = 1.75 GB + 30M customer x 4 B x 3 = 0.36 GB = 60.3 GB, matching the measured 60.34 GB (cn4-transmits.txt); q22: 1.5B x 4 B (o_custkey INT) x 3 = 18 GB vs 18.56 GB measured and a 6.17 GB HASH_JOIN build input per CN (cn4-quent.txt:3875). The join hints exist and work as described at the grammar/optimizer level (StarRocks.g4:2535-2568 bracketHint on joinRelation; AstBuilder.java:6567-6575 setJoinHint; JoinHelper.java:344-349 onlyBroadcast / 148-151 onlyShuffle; RequiredPropertyDeriver.java:140-166), and `broadcast_row_limit <= 0` does force shuffle for every join not exempted by onlyBroadcast (EnforceAndCostTask.java:305-314, exemptions: cross join, NULL_AWARE_LEFT_ANTI, inner join without equi-predicate, HINT_JOIN_BROADCAST). Nothing in the CN or translator overrides the FE cut (engine.rs:551-590 only declares exact stream cardinalities to DuckDB inside a fragment). So the finding is not refuted.

What the source contradicts is the finding's stated mechanism and part of its attribution, which matter for the proposed fixes:

A. The cited code path (CostModel.java:419-441, 'broadcast cost scales with aliveBackendNumber') is not what produces the 1->4 CN flip in this deployment. `ctx.getAliveBackendNumber()` (ConnectContext.java:1497-1503) returns `SystemInfoService.getAliveBackendNumber()` = alive entries of idToBackendRef, i.e. BEs only (SystemInfoService.java:1047-1049, 1123-1132). This cluster runs `run_mode = shared_data` (cn4/cluster.log:201) with four ComputeNodes and no Backend (ids 10001/11001/12002/12003 all logged as `ComputeNode [id=...]` in survey/cluster.log and cn4/cluster.log:939-943; the CN self-registers with `ALTER SYSTEM ADD COMPUTE NODE`, lib.rs:210-212; capture-cn.sh:19 counts `SHOW COMPUTE NODES`). Hence aliveBackendNumber = 0: the BROADCAST exchange cost at line 424-426 is (cpu 0, mem S, net S) -> real cost 3.5 S with the 0.5/2/1.5 weights of getRealCost (CostModel.java:129-135), identical at 1 and 4 CNs. The CN count enters through HashJoinCostModel.getMemCost (HashJoinCostModel.java, `beNum = max(1, aliveBackendNumber + (isSharedDataMode ? aliveComputeNodeNumber : 0))`; memCost = rightOutput x beNum for BROADCAST vs rightOutput for SHUFFLE, weight 2), while parallelFactor = max(0+4, DOP = 144 cores/2 = 72, BackendResourceStat.java:210-212) makes the shuffle build term negligible. With outputRowCount = 1 everywhere (StatisticsCalculator.computeFileScanNode:664-677) Statistics.getOutputSize (Statistics.java:88-108) is just the sum of projected type sizes, so broadcast(right) beats shuffle(both) iff (4+2N) S_r + 0.5 S_l < 4.007 S_r + 2.5 S_l, i.e. S_r < ~S_l at 1 CN and S_r < ~S_l/4 at 4 CNs. This reproduces the observed decisions: q03 build 16 B (o_orderkey 8 + o_orderdate DATE 4 + o_shippriority INT 4) vs probe 24 B -> broadcast at 1 CN, shuffle at 4; q19 1-CN broadcast of the 32 B lineitem projection over the 44 B part projection (p_brand/p_container VARCHAR = 16 each) is predicted by this model and NOT by one where aliveBackendNumber = 1 (that would require S_r < 0.44 S_l and predict shuffle); the surviving 4-CN broadcasts are exactly the narrow builds (q22 o_custkey 4 B, q07 c_custkey+c_nationkey, q02 ps_partkey+min(ps_supplycost)). So 'arithmetic, not data-driven' is right, but the arithmetic is projected row width x shared-data CN count in HashJoinCostModel, not aliveBackendNumber in visitPhysicalDistribution. Confidence: high on the code reading (no BE registered), medium-high on the arithmetic (not executed in the FE; cost debug logging was off).

B. For q07 and q02 the finding attributes the movement to the joins that 'stay BROADCAST'; card-compare-cn4.txt says otherwise. q07 at 4 CN shuffles lineitem 1,822,871,264 rows (exch8, as the BUILD of join 9 against a 799,746-row probe) and orders 1.5B rows (exch13, build of join 14 against 146M) plus 146M twice (exch11/20); the customer broadcast is 600M rows of ~8 B (~3.6 GB of the 69 GB, inference from widths). q02 at 4 CN shuffles the 800M-row partsupp stream four times (exch4, 21, 26, 31) on ps_partkey, ps_suppkey, s_nationkey and n_regionkey to meet builds of 10M (supplier, exch23), 25 (nation, exch28) and 1 (region, exch33) rows; the 472M-row broadcast (exch39) is the smaller mover. The proposed `[SHUFFLE]` hints for q07's customer and q02's subquery side therefore address a minor share; `[BROADCAST]` of the tiny dimension sides is the larger lever in both.

C. EnforceAndCostTask.java:291-296 zeroes the hinted child's cost only when `childCost == Double.POSITIVE_INFINITY` (the broadcast property was otherwise unreachable); the hint's operative effect is JoinHelper.onlyBroadcast -> RequiredPropertyDeriver keeps only the broadcast requirement (RequiredPropertyDeriver.java:148-150).

D. Hint feasibility: bracketHint is only accepted in joinRelation (StarRocks.g4:2535-2541), not in the comma-join `relations` rule (g4:2479-2481); the kit's queries are comma joins over FILES() CTE aliases (queries/qNN.sql lines 2-9 and the FROM lists), so hints require rewriting the FROM clauses into explicit JOIN ... ON. Hints also switch off reorder/commutativity for those joins (ReorderJoinRule.java:70, MultiJoinNode.java:97, JoinCommutativityRule.java:67, JoinAssociativityRule.java:92, SemiReorderRule.java:70), so the rewritten text must also pin the join order and put the intended build on the right; QUERY-DEVIATIONS.md:24-48 already records that the CBO follows the written order at cardinality 1 and that both A/B engines must run identical text.

E. q22 impact: `broadcast_row_limit = 0` turns join 11 into a PARTITIONED LEFT ANTI JOIN (orders shuffled; ~375M rows build per CN), it does not 'remove the 1.5B-row build'; making the ~6M filtered customers the build needs a RIGHT ANTI JOIN, which only JoinCommutativityRule can produce (blocked by any hint) and which the width-only cost model has no reason to prefer. The translator does accept RIGHT_ANTI_JOIN (node_translator.rs:1749).

F. Minor: 'in a 1.418 s query' is the Quent span of q03.r1 (cn4-quent.txt:788); the wall was 1639 ms (cn4-transmits.txt) and the warm median 1607 ms (results.md:5). The efficiency numbers (results-ratios.md) are measured; the causal share of movement in the missing efficiency remains inference, as the finding itself states.

G. An existing (INVISIBLE) knob the finding did not list: `cbo_debug_alive_backend_number` (SessionVariable.java:1823-1824) overrides ctx.getAliveBackendNumber(); it only increases the broadcast penalty and cannot restore size-awareness, so it is not a fix, but it is the only place the CBO's node count can be steered today.
result.corrections:
1. Mechanism: the 1->4 CN flip is not driven by `aliveBackendNumber` in CostModel.visitPhysicalDistribution (CostModel.java:419-441). In this shared_data, CN-only cluster (cn4/cluster.log:201; ComputeNode ids 10001/11001/12002/12003; no Backend) `ctx.getAliveBackendNumber()` = alive BEs = 0 (ConnectContext.java:1497-1503 -> SystemInfoService.java:1047-1049, 1123-1132), so the broadcast exchange cost is (0, S, S) at any CN count. The CN count enters via HashJoinCostModel.getMemCost (beNum = aliveBackendNumber + aliveComputeNodeNumber in shared-data mode; memCost = rightOutput x beNum for BROADCAST, weight 2). With rows = 1 the decision reduces to projected row widths (Statistics.getOutputSize = sum of PrimitiveType.getTypeSize): broadcast the right side iff its width < ~left width at 1 CN, < ~1/4 of the left width at 4 CNs. That is why the surviving 4-CN broadcasts are the narrow-key builds (q22 o_custkey INT 4 B, q07 c_custkey+c_nationkey, q02 ps_partkey+min(ps_supplycost)). Cite HashJoinCostModel.java getMemCost/getCpuCost and Statistics.java:88-108 instead of, or in addition to, CostModel.java:419-441.
2. q07/q02 attribution: the dominant 4-CN movers are partitioned shuffles, not the residual broadcasts — q07 exch8 lineitem 1.82B rows (build vs 800K probe) and exch13 orders 1.5B; q02 exch4/21/26/31 = 4 x 800M partsupp-derived rows re-shuffled to meet 10M/25/1-row builds. The 600M (q07) and 472M (q02) broadcast rows are the smaller share (q07 customer ~3.6 GB of 69 GB, inference from 8 B/row). The stronger per-query lever is `[BROADCAST]` on the small dimension sides, not `[SHUFFLE]` on the customer/subquery sides.
3. EnforceAndCostTask.java:291-296 zeroes the hinted broadcast child's cost only when that cost is +infinity; the hint acts mainly through JoinHelper.onlyBroadcast (JoinHelper.java:344-349) -> RequiredPropertyDeriver.java:148-150.
4. Hints need explicit JOIN syntax (StarRocks.g4:2535-2541, 2565-2568); the kit's comma-join queries (g4:2479-2481; queries/qNN.sql) must be rewritten, and hinted joins are excluded from reorder/commutativity (ReorderJoinRule.java:70, MultiJoinNode.java:97, JoinCommutativityRule.java:67), so the text must also pin order and build side. This is a text deviation the kit tracks (QUERY-DEVIATIONS.md:24-48).
5. q22: `broadcast_row_limit=0` yields a PARTITIONED LEFT ANTI (orders shuffled, ~375M-row build per CN), it does not remove the build; the RIGHT ANTI shape with customers as build is not hint-reachable.
6. 'in a 1.418 s query' is the Quent span (cn4-quent.txt:788); wall 1639 ms, warm median 1607 ms (results.md:5).
7. engine.rs receiver declaration is at lines ~551-590 in this tree (declare_input_cardinality), not 562-595.

result.reasoning: Source check confirms the mechanism; it fails to refute. (1) Sender output repos are created outside the per-query manager: src/exec/streaming_fragment.cpp:103-113 ("Repositories escape data_repository_manager_ cleanup ..."; `_output_repos[id] = std::make_shared<cucascade::shared_data_repository>()`). The only code that registers a repository with the per-query manager is src/pipeline/repository_wiring_materializer.cpp:68 (`add_new_repository` for inter-pipeline ports), and cucascade::data_repository_manager owns repos by unique_ptr (cucascade/include/cucascade/data/data_repository_manager.hpp:108-118), so the sink's shared_ptr repos cannot be in it. The sink writes through batch_stream::push -> `_repo->add_data_batch` (src/exec/batch_stream.cpp:41-52; sink ctor src/op/sirius_physical_streaming_sink.cpp:61-62); nothing subscribes or locks parked batches (no subscribe() in src/exec or the sink/source), so they are idle GPU batches that would be eligible if a sweep ever reached them. (2) The downgrade executor sweeps only `_data_repo_registry.get_all()` managers (src/downgrade/downgrade_executor.cpp:223-232) and the pipeline task queue (:294-300, `has_matching_batches` - queued GPU_SCAN tasks hold no input batches), so it never sees these repos; the disk warning at :357-363 fires on `disk_not_configured && !satisfied && !is_monitor_request` regardless of whether any candidate existed - the claim about misleading attribution is correct. (3) Measured: cn1/engine-cn0.log, q05 window 13:03:43-13:05:25: 2503 "downgrade request not satisfied ... disk" lines and 2503 "after downgrade (0 bytes freed)" lines (finding's count is exact); whole log 17917 such lines, none with non-zero bytes freed; 6 "exceeded ... retries". `[gpu_pool] GPU:0 QueryEnd window=78 query=219` (the q05 lineitem sender, 13:03:43.434 -> 13:05:24.624 = 101.2 s = q05.r0 101460 ms) shows allocated=104297693440 peak=107374182400 (the 100 GiB cap). HOST tier exists (`[host_pool] HOST:0 ... peak=33991688192`, capture-cn.sh:11 HOST_MEM=160GiB -> engine_settings.rs:111-116 `sirius.memory.host.capacity_bytes`). (4) No existing knob covers it: the CN accepts `--sirius-config` (main.rs:72) so a DISK tier could be configured, but a DISK target only adds a target space; TIER 1/2 would still yield zero candidates. The monitor path (should_downgrade_memory is allocation-based, cucascade/src/memory/memory_space.cpp:292-296) fires too but sweeps the same two tiers and logs only at DEBUG - consistent with the log (inference). (5) Proposed change is feasible where proposed: a process-level shared_ptr/weak_ptr registry swept with the same convertible_data_batch_provider(repo*) works on these repos; HOST conversions go through the reservation-taking convert path already used elsewhere. Two corrections below, neither of which overturns the claim.
result.corrections: (A) The clause "the sender's engine query has already ended" is not the operative reason in the measured failures. In q05 the 104.3 GB that filled the pool is the RUNNING lineitem sender's own STREAMING_SINK output (cn1-quent.txt:353-355: fragment ...5774 STREAMING_SINK n=40 in=104.30GB while its GPU_SCAN tasks were still OOM-rescheduling; gpu_pool window 78 allocated=104297693440 at its QueryEnd). That query's manager existed (sirius_context.cpp:393 create_for_query) but held zero repositories because a single-pipeline scan->sink fragment has no inter-pipeline wiring. The escape from the manager (streaming_fragment.cpp:103-113) is the whole mechanism; the query-ended path (sirius_ffi.cpp:1025-1026 lifecycle->finish() -> sirius_context.cpp:591-603 -> :436 erase) only covers outputs parked after run(), which in q05 were 0.00-1.24 GB each (cn1-quent.txt:347-360). The 0 "un-consumed data batch" leak warnings in the window are consistent: erase() never saw these repos. Same pattern for q08 (sink in=99.54GB), q09 (96.42GB), q17 (66.26GB), q18 (35.87GB), q21 (25.37GB). (B) The proposed "make relay_from accept HOST-tier batches (re-materialise on push)" is unnecessary for the local relay: relay_from only moves shared_ptr handles (sirius_ffi.cpp:785-797), and the receiver's task input path already upgrades HOST/DISK batches to GPU (pipelineable_operator_data::prepare_for_processing -> lock_or_prepare_batch, src/op/sirius_physical_operator.cpp:98; batch_lock_utils.hpp "HOST/DISK -> GPU upgrade/readback"). What does need HOST-tier support: Fragment::output_row_count (sirius_ffi.cpp:1062-1066) - note the CN already swallows that throw via `.ok()` and falls back to "input stream row count unknown; planning without a declared cardinality" (engine.rs:564, 582-585), so today it degrades planning rather than failing - and Fragment::export_packed (sirius_ffi.cpp:822-825), which throws and would fail the 4-CN path. host_data_representation exposes no generic row count (only column_metadata.hpp:42 num_rows per column via get_host_table()), so "count rows from metadata" needs a small accessor. (C) The proposed sweep order "oldest parked query first" conflicts with the existing newest-first fairness policy (downgrade_executor.cpp:204-216) and would not select the candidate that matters here: the newest, still-running fragment's own sink output. (D) The impact numbers 97.5/122/244 GB are the standalone GPU_SCAN projection sizes from agent-notes/oom-failures.md's table, not measured parked bytes; the arithmetic against ~160 GiB HOST minus the ~34 GB pinned-pool peak still supports "host spill rescues only q17/q18 (maybe q21)", so the conclusion stands but should be labelled as an estimate.

result.reasoning:
The CLAIM (mechanism) is confirmed from the source and the log; the PROPOSED CHANGE and one impact statement are contradicted at the code level, and the headline number needs correcting. Verdict: not refuted as a finding, but (b) and (c) of the proposal should be dropped or re-scoped and (a) needs an arena-capacity caveat.

CONFIRMED (measured facts):
1. Single dispatch worker joins drains before the next queued fragment: /home/prestouser/aocsa/sirius-stacks-wt/perf/experimental/starrocks/src/compute_node_service.rs:380-392 (dispatch_worker, one std thread, `queue.extend(core.run_ready_fragment(ready))`), :864-872 (`.and_then(FragmentOutcome::join_into_ready)`), :160-163 (`self.drains.join()?`), :104-128 (SenderDrains::join joins EVERY ticket). Sender-only fragments landed on that worker because capture-cn.sh:12 exported SIRIUS_CN_ASYNC_SENDER_DISPATCH=1 (opt-in from commit 9a5a4da6; try_dispatch_sender -> dispatch -> inbox). Log: cn4/cluster.log q03.r1, last transmit of 5f at 13:19:45.611449, customer scan 5b 'fragment run started' at 45.611674 (0.2 ms later); same on 9122 (45.620620 -> 45.620796), 9112 (45.662060 -> 45.662242), 9132 (45.688072 -> 45.688266).
2. One transport thread, destinations drained one at a time in FE order, each batch = export_packed_next -> rpc_request_lease -> write_and_wait -> rpc_transmit -> staging_release: nixl_transport.rs:397-418 (transport_thread handles SendFragment inline), :713-775 (drain loop), :227-243 (start_fragment posts to the FIFO), compute_node_service.rs:1207-1219 (comment).
3. The pack runs on the engine thread: engine.rs:813 export_packed_next = engine_call; engine.rs:321-324 ExportNext arm inside the single `while let Ok(request) = requests.recv()` loop (engine.rs:284-330); export_next (engine.rs:380-403) -> Fragment::export_packed (src/sirius_ffi.cpp:803-887) which does cudf::chunked_pack with kPackChunkBytes = 8 MiB (:800) on cudf::get_default_stream() and stream.synchronize() (:876) before returning.
4. Post-finish drain span per CN: transmits at +95/+190/+283 ms after 'finished' (log lines above; cn4-transmits.txt q03.r1 elapsed max 96 ms, write max 8 ms).

CONTRADICTED / CORRECTED:
A. '92% of each transmit is the pack' -> measured 84%. The staging-arena Quent probe times the pack directly (staging_arena_telemetry.hpp:49 'export_packed stationary => in_transit => stationary'; on_pack_started/on_pack_completed at sirius_ffi.cpp:861/880). From cn4/quent/.cn0-3/*/data_batch for the q03.r1 sender fragments: 51-52 sender-side leases >100 MB per CN, 15.27-15.35 GB, pack (InTransit->Stationary) median 4.88-4.90 ms per ~300 MB lease = 63.5-64.0 GB/s, summed 237.9-239.7 ms per CN against a ~285 ms three-destination drain (3 x 93-96 ms) => 84%. Per-batch cycle (inter-lease start gap) median 5.89 ms: 4.9 ms pack + 0.7 ms lease-held non-pack (lease RPC + WRITE + transmit RPC) + ~0.3 ms release/channel hop. The finding's 92% attributes the transmit RPC and release overhead to the pack.
B. Proposals (b) 'one transport thread per peer so the 3 destinations drain concurrently' and (c) 'start the next queued sender while a drain is in flight' cannot deliver the claimed 0.15-0.3 s: every ExportNext AND every fragment Run go through the same single engine thread (engine.rs:284-330; run_fragment_inner calls fragment.run() synchronously at engine.rs:~684; Fragment::run blocks until the pipeline finishes, src/sirius_ffi.cpp:990-1027). With three transport threads the packs (84% of the drain, 239 ms/CN) still serialise on that thread; with a non-joining dispatch worker the next fragment's Run (customer scan 35-43 ms) would sit in the same FIFO as the remaining ExportNext calls, so the drain is delayed by the scan rather than overlapped. Upper bound of (b)+(c) alone is the non-pack part, ~45 ms per CN on q03 (0.7 ms x 52 leases + hops), not 0.15-0.3 s.
C. Impact sentence 'a further ~0.3 s is small fragments that could have overlapped the lineitem scan' is contradicted by the same code: the CN engine runs exactly one fragment at a time (one engine thread, Run arm holds it for the whole fragment.run()); there is no concurrent-fragment path in engine.rs, and this is independent of the dispatch worker. Only the ~16% non-engine part of a drain could ever overlap a fragment.
D. Proposal (a) first variant ('STREAMING_SINK could pack each batch straight into a staging lease' during execution) is infeasible at the campaign's arena size: sender-side packed output is 15.3 GB per CN (Quent, above) while the receiver-side leases of the same query hold 14.5-14.6 GB for 437-684 ms (median held 437-595 ms) and the measured whole-query arena occupancy already peaks at 14.95-15.10 GB of the 17.18 GB (16 GiB, capture-cn.sh:11 SIRIUS_EXCHANGE_STAGING_BYTES=16GiB) at +1.28 s. Holding both sets would need ~30 GB; exchange_staging_arena::lease throws 'exchange staging arena exhausted' (src/exec/exchange_staging_arena.cpp:247-258), export_packed rethrows, nixl_transport.rs:713 `?` fails the drain and :407-418 drops the parked output — no wait/retry. It would require >= 2x SIRIUS_EXCHANGE_STAGING_BYTES or a blocking lease. Also STREAMING_SINK has no remote/local knowledge: the Fragment FFI only exposes declare_output_hash_key / declare_output_broadcast (src/include/sirius_ffi.hpp:240-300) and Local vs Remote routing is decided in Rust after translation (compute_node_service.rs route_destination, ~:1235-1260), so the sink would need a new per-output declaration. The second variant (run export_packed on a dedicated thread) is the one that addresses the real serialisation point but needs ParkedOutput/Fragment to be reachable off the engine thread (parked HashMap lives on the engine thread's stack, engine.rs:262-272).
E. 'Quent wall 1.28 s vs CN elapsed 0.61-0.68 s (the difference is parked/drain lifetime)': the drain ends at +0.893 s (45.611449); the parked output is released only when the LOCAL receiver 53 relays it at 46.014522 (+1.296 s, 'relayed native batches ... stream_id=2 sender_id=0 batches=16'), which matches the 1.280 s Quent wall. So of the 0.67 s difference, 0.28 s is drain and 0.39 s is waiting for the local receiver's rendezvous (it needs all 4 orders x customer senders, which finish 45.91-46.01). The drain is the minority of the parked lifetime.
F. Contingency not stated in the finding: the 'next queued fragment waits for the drain on the dispatch worker' shape exists only because SIRIUS_CN_ASYNC_SENDER_DISPATCH=1 (off by default, 9a5a4da6). With the default, a sender runs inline in its exec_plan_fragment RPC (compute_node_service.rs:~703-712 exec_single_attachment -> dispatch_then_join) and the FE Deployer deploys per stage and waits for each stage's RPCs (Deployer.java:236-243 deployAsync + waitForDeploymentCompletion :318), so the customer scan would be held back by the same drain via the FE instead. The drain is on the critical path either way; the finding should say so.

NET: the serialised post-finish drain is real and ~0.28 s of q03's 1.42 s span at 4 CN; the fix must move or shrink the pack itself (it is the engine-thread-serial 84%), and (a)'s arena cost must be budgeted. (b)/(c) as written are not effective changes.
result.corrections:
1) Pack share of the per-destination transmit: 84% measured (239 ms of ~285 ms per CN; 4.9 ms per ~300 MB lease, 63.5 GB/s), not 92% (the finding's residual includes the transmit RPC + release + engine channel hop, ~1 ms/batch).
2) Proposals (b) and (c) do not yield the stated 0.15-0.3 s: export_packed and fragment Run share ONE engine thread (engine.rs:284-330), so packs serialise regardless of transport thread count and a non-joining dispatch worker only reorders Run vs ExportNext in the same FIFO; realistic upper bound ~45 ms/CN on q03.
3) Impact claim that the customer/orders x customer fragments 'could have overlapped the lineitem scan' is wrong for the current engine: one fragment at a time per CN by design (single engine thread, synchronous Fragment::run at sirius_ffi.cpp:990-1027).
4) Proposal (a) variant 'pack into staging leases during execution' needs ~30 GB of arena per CN for q03 (15.3 GB sender-side + 14.5 GB receiver-side held 0.44-0.68 s) against 17.18 GB configured; exhaustion is a hard failure (exchange_staging_arena.cpp:247-258, nixl_transport.rs:713/407-418). State the SIRIUS_EXCHANGE_STAGING_BYTES requirement (>= 32 GiB) or add a blocking lease; STREAMING_SINK also has no remote/local hint today (FFI has only declare_output_hash_key/declare_output_broadcast; routing is in compute_node_service.rs route_destination).
5) 'Quent wall 1.28 s - CN elapsed 0.61 s = parked/drain lifetime': only 0.28 s of the 0.67 s is drain; 0.39 s is waiting for the local receiver relay at 46.014522.
6) The dispatch-worker serialisation is contingent on SIRIUS_CN_ASYNC_SENDER_DISPATCH=1 (capture-cn.sh:12; default off). Under the default the same drain delays the FE's next deploy stage instead (Deployer.java:236-243, :318). Either way it is on the critical path; the finding should name both paths.
7) Confidence on the mechanism: high (code + log). Confidence on the 'expected gain 0.15-0.3 s': only reachable if the pack is moved off the engine thread or made much faster; with (b)+(c) alone it is low.

1. "92% of each per-destination transmit is the pack": the log arithmetic (95-1-6)/95 lumps the per-batch RPC/handshake overhead into "pack". The Quent probe measures pack = 84-88% for q03 (4.9 ms pack + 0.7 ms send + ~0.3 ms ExportNext round-trip/release per 311 MB batch), 74-81% for q10 (130 MB batches), 75-82% for q12 (640 MB batches), and only 18-32% for q19 (7 MB batches: pack 0.15 ms vs send 0.32 ms). The pack-bound statement is correct for q03/q10/q12 but does not hold for q19, which the claim lists; for small batches the fixed per-batch cost (~0.5-0.9 ms: lease RPC, write, transmit RPC, ExportNext round trip) dominates. Pack throughput is a flat ~63-65 GB/s for batches >= 100 MB.
2. "All 16 fragment RPCs of q03 arrived within 44.708-44.719": 13 exec_plan_fragment closes at 44.708283-44.719506 and 4 at 44.765257-44.765368 (a second FE deploy wave). Conclusion unchanged: all arrived >= 0.85 s before the drains ended.
3. Impact: "a further ~0.3 s is small fragments that could have overlapped the lineitem scan" is not achievable under any of the proposed changes: the engine serves one Run request at a time (engine.rs:280 loop; Run is synchronous), so the customer scan (35-42 ms) and orders x customer (185-277 ms) can never overlap the lineitem scan on the same CN. They could only overlap the drain, and only if the pack leaves the engine thread. The achievable saving is the drain itself, ~0.25-0.28 s of the 1.42 s span for q03 (consistent with the proposal's own 0.15-0.3 s estimate), not 0.55 s.
4. Proposal (c) "it already dispatches ready receivers first; extend that to queued senders": on the async-dispatch path actually used (SIRIUS_CN_ASYNC_SENDER_DISPATCH=1), join_into_ready (compute_node_service.rs:160-163) joins the drains BEFORE yielding ready receivers; dispatch-before-join exists only on the inline RPC path (dispatch_then_join, :337-360). And (c) alone gains nothing: a sender started during the drain competes with ExportNext for the single engine thread, and its own SendFragment requests queue behind the in-flight drains on the single transport FIFO, so the orders x customer receivers (which need all 4 CNs' customer frames) start no earlier. (c) needs (a) or (b).
5. "Quent wall 1.28 s vs CN elapsed 0.61-0.68 s (the difference is parked/drain lifetime)": the Quent Query Exit for ec5f is 46.014480, coinciding with the local receiver ec53's Init 46.014262 (the local slot's release drops the parked fragment), not with the drain end at 45.611. 6. Per-transmit elapsed is 92-98 ms across the three q03 runs (claim: 93-96); write_gbps 597-717. Trivial.

For q10 join 13 (build 114.7M rows) the guard rejects broadcast under both exact and row-count-only stats (customer x nation 13.8 GB < 114.7M x 20 B x 10 = 22.9 GB). Only q12 (est 11.7M rows, guard off) and q19 flip to BROADCAST. So the remedy as written removes ~26 GB (q12 + q19 + possibly q10's lineitem shuffle) of the ~135 GB it claims, not the 60 GB q03 / 19 GB q10-customer flows that dominate its impact section. (d) Impact percentages: q12 is 11% (0.12/1.08), outside the stated 15-25%; the '0.5 s arena dwell' is not additive to wall time (it overlaps the customer and orders x customer fragments that are on the critical path in either plan); q19/q14 show no measurable wall effect (drains 4-6% of span; q19's 2.14x speed-up equals join-free q06's 2.25x within noise and exceeds q14's 2.11x), so 'moves 45x more bytes' for q19 is a byte count, not a cost.

1. Sub-claim 'at 1 CN every join is BROADCAST' is wrong. survey/plan-summary.txt (1 CN) has PARTITIONED or BUCKET_SHUFFLE joins in q02 q05 q07 q08 q09 q13 q17 q18 q20 q21 (lines 10, 14, 16, 18, 26, 34, 36, 40, 42); only q03 q04 q10 q11 q12 q14 q15 q16 q19 q22 are all-BROADCAST at 1 CN. Reword to 'for this family (q03/q10/q12/q14/q19) every join is BROADCAST at 1 CN'.

2. Mechanism attribution (evidence item 1, code_refs CostModel.java:401-432). In this cluster the CNs are COMPUTE NODEs (src/lib.rs:211 'ALTER SYSTEM ADD COMPUTE NODE'; FE log 'ComputeNode [id=10001..12003]' in survey/cluster.log and cn4/cluster.log). ConnectContext.getAliveBackendNumber() -> SystemInfoService.getAliveBackendNumber() = getBackendIds(true).size() over idToBackendRef only (SystemInfoService.java:1047-1048, 1123-1128; addComputeNode puts into idToComputeNodeRef, :174), so aliveBackendNumber = 0, beNum = 1, and the BROADCAST exchange cost is (cpu 0, mem R, net R) = 3.5R independent of N. The N-scaling that flips q03's orders join comes from HashJoinCostModel.getMemCost (fe-core/.../cost/HashJoinCostModel.java, memCost = rightOutput x beNum where beNum = aliveBE + aliveCN in shared_data mode; the FE runs shared_data per configs/gb200-4gpu/cluster4-numa.sh:231) weighted 2, plus parallelFactor = aliveBE + aliveCN in getCpuCost. With cardinality 1 everywhere this reduces to: broadcast iff probeWidth > buildWidth x (N - 0.25/N); at N=4 q03 lineitem 24 B vs orders x customer 16 B -> 24 < 63 -> shuffle; customer 4 B vs orders 20 B -> 20 > 15.75 -> broadcast (matches both 4-CN plans). Also note the 1-CN survey was not 'single node' to the FE: four CNs (10001, 11001, 12002, 12003) were registered with one alive, so isSingleBackendAndComputeNode() (SystemInfoService.java:246-248, counts registered not alive) was false and SHUFFLE network cost was charged; that is why broadcast won at 1 CN for this family. The same code paths make checkBroadcastRowCountLimit use beNum = 1 here, not 4.

3. Proposed change outcome. 'Even a row-count-only estimate re-arms checkBroadcastRowCountLimit (15M) ... so q03/q10/q12/q19 would broadcast the filtered small side' is contradicted for q03 and q10: re-arming the guard makes the FE REFUSE to broadcast a >15M-row side unless the probe is >10x larger in bytes. Row-count-only (columns UNKNOWN): q03 build est = max(orders 1.5B x 0.25, customer 150M x 0.25) = 375M rows (StatisticsCalculator.java:1231-1243), probe 1.5B x 24 B = 36 GB < 375M x 16 B x 10 = 60 GB -> pruned at EnforceAndCostTask.java:184/315-320. Exact stats: 145.8M rows, probe 77.6 GB > 23.3 GB passes the guard, but HashJoinCostModel's probe cache penalty (broadcast min(12, ln(145.8M/1e5)) = 7.28 vs shuffle min(3, ...) = 3) gives broadcast ~315 vs shuffle ~286 cost units -> still PARTITIONED. q10 join 13 (lineitem x orders 114.7M rows as build): guard rejects under both (customer x nation 150M x 92 B = 13.8 GB < 22.9 GB). q12 (est 11.7M < 15M) and q19 (part-filtered est a few M) do flip to BROADCAST. Corrected expectation: the FILES() row-count fix alone recovers q12 (23.5 -> 1.5 GB) and q19 (2.75 -> 0.06 GB), ~26 GB of the ~135 GB 'excess'; q03 (60 GB) and q10's customer shuffle (19.2 GB) additionally require raising broadcast_row_count_limit / broadcast_right_table_scale_factor (SessionVariable.java:1833-1836) and neutralising the CPU-cache penalty in HashJoinCostModel (BOTTOM_NUMBER=100000, BROADCAST_MAT_RATIO=12, SHUFFLE_MAX_RATIO=3), or moving the decision to the CN. Confidence on the code reading: high; the cost arithmetic is a hand computation (no FE debug log), medium.

4. Impact numbers. Drains as a share of span: q03 0.283-0.287/1.435 = 20%; q10 0.255-0.285/1.478 = 17-19% (finding says 0.24); q12 0.115-0.125/1.081 = 11% (outside the stated 15-25%); q19 4-6%; q14 5%. '0.28 s/CN drain + 0.5 s arena dwell out of a 1.42 s span' double counts: the dwell (frames land +0.71..+1.01 s, consumed +1.30 s) is the receiver waiting for the customer and orders x customer fragments, which are on the critical path in the broadcast plan too; it is a memory-occupancy cost (88% of the 16 GiB arena), not wall time. The alternative plan also has uncosted work the finding omits: each CN must build the full 145.8M-row (2.33 GB) hash table (4x redundant build) and its lineitem scan cannot start until that side is parked (receiver-first rendezvous, fact 2), whereas today the lineitem scan starts at t=0. My critical-path estimate for the broadcast plan is ~1.1-1.2 s vs 1.435 s measured, so the '0.2-0.4 s per query' gain is plausible for q03 but is an inference, and for q19/q14 the gain is ~0.

5. 'The natural plan (the 1-CN shape generalised)' should be labelled as DuckDB's single-node shape, not what a statistics-aware StarRocks FE produces at 4 nodes (see 3).
extra_evidence: Per-CN drain is strictly serial and on the critical path: cn4/cluster.log q03.r1 sender ec5f (127.0.0.1:9102) finished +0.610 s (L10339), transmits complete +0.705/+0.799/+0.893 (L10429, L10571, L10715), next fragment ec5b on 9102 starts +0.893 (L10732); same pattern on 9132 (ec61 finish +0.684, last tx +0.969, ec5d start +0.970).

Each ~4.85 GB frame: elapsed_ms 92-96, lease_ms 1-2, write_ms 6-8 (600-717 GB/s) => ~87 ms of each drain is CPU-side pack/export, not NVLink transfer; the byte volume matters via pack time, not link bandwidth.
